text:
Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on a flight in the US, as long as it goes in your carry-on and not your checked bag.

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limits lithium-ion power banks to 100 Wh per battery. [FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)
- To get watt-hours, divide mAh by 1000 and multiply by the voltage. Most power banks use about 3.7 V cells, so 20,000 mAh works out to roughly 74 Wh, well under the limit. (The 3.7 V figure is my assumption. Check the Wh printed on your battery.)
- Spare batteries and power banks must be in carry-on only. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. [FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)

**Tips**
- Protect the terminals from short circuits. Use the original packaging, a pouch, or tape over the ports.
- Don't fly with a damaged or recalled battery.
- If it gets hot, swells, or smokes, tell the crew right away.
- Airlines can set stricter limits, including how many power banks you can bring. The FAA says to check with your carrier before you travel.
- TSA security rules are separate from the FAA's safety rules, but a power bank under 100 Wh in your carry-on is the standard permitted case. [FAA PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank)

The Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, about 74 Wh, 100 W USB-C output) is listed as carry-on legal and costs $89.99: [Baseus Blade H1](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah).
